questions.text: Which best describes your work arrangement over the past 12 months?
options: Fully remote (zero required in-office days)
Predominantly remote (1 required in-office day per week or less)

questions.text: How long have you been working primarily remotely (≤1 day per week in office)?
options: Less than 1 year
1–2 years
3–4 years
5+ years (started during COVID or earlier and stayed)

questions.text: In the past 12 months, have you done any of the following because the in-person component felt uncomfortable, exhausting, or anxiety-inducing?
options: Declined a job interview that required showing up in person
Withdrew from a hiring process when I learned it was on-site
Skipped a professional networking event that could have helped my career
Avoided applying for a promotion that involves managing people in person
Avoided applying for a role with any in-office or hybrid requirements
Skipped a work conference or industry event
Declined to present, lead a meeting, or speak in front of a group
Turned down a client-facing assignment
None of the above

questions.text: Would you accept lower pay in order to keep working fully remotely?
options: Yes, I would accept more than 20% less
Yes, I would accept 10–20% less
Yes, I would accept less than 10% less
No, I would not accept less pay to stay remote

questions.text: If your company announced a mandatory return to office (5 days per week) starting next month, how prepared would you feel to handle it socially and emotionally?
options: Very prepared
Somewhat prepared
Somewhat unprepared
Very unprepared
I would quit before returning

questions.text: How often do you have unscripted, in-person interactions with someone outside your household in a typical week?
options: 0 times
1–2 times
3–5 times
6–10 times
More than 10 times

questions.text: Have you done any of the following because a work interaction felt too exhausting, awkward, or anxiety-inducing?
options: Pretended my camera or microphone was broken
"Forgot" to join a meeting I could have attended
Kept my camera off when I was supposed to have it on
Sent a message when I should have called
Called in sick to avoid an in-person event
Asked a colleague to attend in my place
Faked a scheduling conflict
Avoided eye contact during video calls
None of the above

questions.text: In the past 12 months, have you used AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) for any of these communication needs you would have handled on your own before working remotely?
options: Drafting a difficult work message (asking for a raise, pushing back, conflict)
Practicing what to say in an interview
Writing a LinkedIn outreach or networking message
Rehearsing a difficult conversation before having it
Translating my feelings into "professional" language
Drafting a sympathy or condolence note to a colleague
Coming up with small-talk or networking openers
None of the above

questions.text: Compared to job interviews you did before you started working remotely, how do in-person interviews compare for you now?
options: I haven't done an in-person interview since I went remote
They go better now
About the same
They go somewhat worse
They go significantly worse

questions.text: When job-searching today, do you filter out roles that would require in-person work?
options: Yes — I filter out anything that isn't fully remote
Yes — I filter out anything more than 1 office day per week
Somewhat — I'd consider in-person for the right role and pay
No — I apply broadly regardless of location
I'm not currently job-searching
